summary: This Dockerfile builds an Ubuntu container with an enhanced Zsh shell environment. It installs Zsh and essential tools, sets up Oh-My-Zsh with a plugin for SSH config auto-completion, creates a sample SSH config file with predefined hosts, customizes the shell prompt to show a container indicator, and starts the shell in interactive login mode.

explanations.3: This tells Ubuntu's package manager to skip interactive prompts during installation—otherwise the build would hang waiting for user input.
explanations.5: The && chains commands together so if any step fails, the whole RUN stops. After installing packages, we delete the cached package lists to reduce the image size.
explanations.11: Removing /var/lib/apt/lists/* cleans up the package manager's download cache, which saves disk space in the final image since we won't need it again.
explanations.14: This downloads and runs Oh-My-Zsh's installer script directly from GitHub using curl, with --unattended to run non-interactively.
explanations.18: The --depth=1 flag clones only the latest commit of the plugin repo instead of the entire history, which is faster and uses less disk space.
explanations.20: This uses sed to find the line starting with 'plugins=(git)' and replaces it with the same line but adding the new plugin name to the list.
explanations.25: The printf command with '%s\n' outputs each argument as a separate line, which is a clean way to build a multi-line file inside the RUN command.
explanations.42: chmod 600 sets permissions so only the owner can read/write the SSH config file, which is a security requirement for SSH.
explanations.47: The -i flag makes the shell interactive and -l makes it a login shell, so it reads startup configuration files and behaves like a normal user shell.
